issues: The two wind turbines are not 'on either side' of the road. One stands near the image centre, just east of the bend in the main road. The other is in the southwest at the road's end, at the turbine pad.
The structured claim puts both turbines in the 'west' cell, but one is in the centre cell and the other is in the southwest.
The main road does not just 'run through the center'. It is a wide graded dirt road that comes in at the top centre, curves southwest and ends at the southwest turbine.
The caption leaves out several narrower dirt tracks that cross the scene, in the north, east and south.
The caption doesn't say the scene is a wind farm or describe the scattered shrubs and trees on dry grassland, so it is vague.
There is only one large warehouse building, and it spans the north edge. The claim of 3 buildings in the north-west is wrong.
No buildings are visible in the south. The south edge holds a lot of parked trailers or vehicles.
The striped parking lot is in the north-west next to the warehouse, not in the west. There is also a large paved truck court north-centre and north-east that the caption doesn't mention.
The 'small solar arrays' in the south-west look like rows of parked truck trailers or vehicles, not solar panels.
The vegetation claim is weak: the site is mostly bare graded dirt with very little vegetation.
The caption leaves out the large rectangular retention or detention basin in the south-centre.
The centre 'field' is a graded, bare-earth construction pad rather than an undeveloped field. The caption doesn't mention that it is being prepared for development.
The solar array covers most of the image, from the north edge to near the south edge and across the east side. Calling it 'in the center' understates how far it extends.
Vegetation is not only to the north and east. Shrubland also appears in the northwest corner, the southeast, and along the southern edge.

Bare ground is mostly the cleared patch west of the northern array block (west-central). The south of the image is mostly array rows and scrub, not bare ground, so the 'south' part of the claim and the south_of relation are weak.
The caption leaves out that the array is two blocks separated by an east-west access road, and that there are inverter or equipment pads along that road.
The caption leaves out the diagonal northeast boundary and the perimeter road around the facility.
The field is placed in the wrong cell. The bare or fallow field is in the north-west (top-left), not the south-west; the south-west is covered in solar panels.
The relation 'field south_of west solar array' is wrong because the field lies to the north of the western panels.
Omission: there is a patch of bare or disturbed ground in the south-east corner.
Omission: the caption doesn't mention the internal access roads that divide the arrays into blocks.
The caption describes the solar farm as four separate large arrays, but the panels form one continuous facility covering most of the image, including the south and south-west.

The structured claims list 2 turbines in the west plus 1 in the centre, which makes 3. The image shows only 2 (one in the centre, one in the west/southwest), so the claims contradict both the caption text and the image.
The caption mentions only one road. The image shows a wide graded light-coloured road curving from the north edge to the west, plus several other dirt tracks and service roads crossing the scene.
Calling the area a 'desert' is loose. It looks like dry grassland or semi-arid rangeland with scattered shrubs and trees.
The vegetation count of 100 is an arbitrary estimate, and placing it only in the centre is wrong because it is scattered across the whole image.
The caption leaves out the turbines' long shadows pointing east-northeast, the blades, and the turbine pads at the ends of the access roads.

The main feature is missed: a large warehouse or distribution building with a roof that spans the north and north-east of the image. The caption says only 'several buildings in the north-west'; the north-west actually holds a paved car park.
There is no building in the south-west. That area is a paved parking or truck lot with vehicles or trailers.
The 'large rectangular structure in the centre' is really an excavated stormwater detention basin, a sunken earthen pit, in the south-centre. It is not a structure.
The paved truck apron and loading area south of the warehouse is not mentioned.
The paved road on the south side is doubtful. The southern edge shows a parking lot and dirt tracks rather than a clear paved road.
The scene is a graded construction or development site, not a natural field. The 'vegetation patches' are mostly sparse scrub and erosion-control rows.

Layout is misdescribed. The facility is two large contiguous blocks: a northern block covering the north-centre, centre and east, and a southern block running across the south and south-west. It is not one large central/eastern array plus smaller western arrays.
There are no distinct 'smaller arrays in the west'. The west-centre is a large cleared bare-ground area with no panels, and only the south-west holds panel rows, as part of the big southern block.
Omission: the NE corner has the densest shrub/tree vegetation in the image, but it is not mentioned.
The NW corner is mostly scrubland with scattered shrubs. The main bare ground is the cleared strip in the west-centre, which the caption does not identify.
Some relations don't make sense: 'vegetation north_of bare_ground' in the NW, and 'vegetation south_of bare_ground' in the SE.
Omission: the access roads/tracks between panel blocks and the inverter/equipment pads are not mentioned.
Bare ground is in the wrong places: it is in the northwest corner (a fallow field) and a small patch in the southeast corner. The caption puts it to the west and south.
The south and southwest are mostly covered by solar panels, not bare ground.
The solar array covers almost the whole image, including the southwest and south. It is not confined to the centre and east.
The caption leaves out the network of dirt access roads that splits the array into blocks, and wrongly says there are no other objects.
The structured claims split one continuous array into two separate solar_array objects.
The second wind turbine sits near the centre of the image, not in the north-east. Only its shadow extends toward the north-east.

The caption mentions only one dirt road, but there are several unpaved roads and tracks, including a wide graded road that curves from the top centre down to the west and south-west, plus other tracks running north–south and east.
'Desert' is somewhat inaccurate: the land looks like dry, semi-arid grassland or rangeland with scattered shrubs and trees.
The vegetation is scattered across the whole image, not concentrated in the centre, and there are likely more than 50 plants.
The east_of and west_of relations to 'the road' are ambiguous because there are several roads, and the central turbine sits between them.
The 'solar array in the west' is not supported by the image. The textured strip in the west looks like graded ground, gravel, or erosion-control rows, not solar panels.
The caption leaves out the large parking lots in the north and northwest next to the warehouse building.
The caption leaves out the large rectangular detention basin in the south-centre of the site.
The 'parking lot in the south' is really a lined lot or truck yard along the southern edge, mostly in the south-west and south-centre. 'South' is acceptable but not exact.
The building is a large warehouse in the north-east and north. The caption could describe it more specifically.
The solar array covers most of the image, from the north edge to the south and from west to east, not only the centre. The caption understates how much of the scene it fills.
The 'bare_ground' claim at east is doubtful: the east cell is mostly solar panels, and the main cleared bare area is in the west and centre-west.
The caption omits the shrub/tree vegetation in the north-east, which is the most vegetated corner.

The caption leaves out the array's layout: an upper block with a diagonal north-east edge, a lower block whose south-east boundary is curved, and an internal access road between them, plus small equipment pads.
The caption is generic and adds no specific detail.
Understates how far the solar array extends: the panels cover almost the whole image (north, south, west, southwest and the centre), not mainly the centre and east.
Leaves out the internal access roads/gravel tracks that split the array into blocks, including the inverter pads along the central east–west road.
The relation 'o3 north_of o1' is loose: the bare field lies northwest of the array and runs along the array's western edge.
